items.headline: Longview Nippon Dynawave Paper Mill Implosion Day 6 — 11 Confirmed Dead (WA's Deadliest Industrial Disaster Since 1930); Victims Identified Saturday; Columbia River Contamination Ongoing; CSB Investigation; OPB: 'Something Dramatically Wrong'; March 2026 Pre-Warning to WA DOLI
items.summary: The Longview, Washington Nippon Dynawave Packaging paper mill white-liquor tank implosion advances to Day 6. On May 26, at approximately 7:15 AM PDT, a 900,000-gallon white liquor tank (sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide) imploded at the Nippon Paper-owned facility on the Columbia River in Cowlitz County. On Saturday May 30, officials formally identified all 11 victims: Gilbert Bernal (52), Tyler Covington (29), Bradley Covington (27), Robert Wilson (48), Dale Miller (54), Jared Ammons (35), Braydon Finkas (38), Clinton Doran (26), John Forsberg (51), Norman Barlow (58), and Dillon Miller. Seven additional workers sustained burns and inhalation injuries; one firefighter was injured. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson characterized the event as 'the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history' — confirmed as the state's deadliest industrial disaster since 1930 (Carbonado mine explosion, 17 killed). Columbia River contamination: corrosive chemicals spilled into the river; dead carp recovered from dikes along the Columbia; EPA Region 10 and WA Department of Ecology monitoring ongoing. US Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (CSB) opened a formal investigation. OPB May 30: 'Something dramatically wrong — questions but few answers' — noting that in March 2026, mill workers notified Washington state's Division of Occupational Safety and Health that a drain hole was creating a sinkhole in the floor, raising pre-warning regulatory compliance questions that will define the investigation timeline. Longview is a major industrial and port community in Cowlitz County, WA (~40 miles north of Portland on the Columbia River). Downstream implications: lower Columbia commercial and tribal fisheries, drinking water intakes, and aquatic ecology on watch.
